name: P2 · Unit 9 — Data Communication & Networks
description: 5 of 14 topics so far (10 sets × 30 questions): Data Communication – Part 1; Data Communication – Part 2; Computer Networks & Topologies; Network Models; Data Link Layer. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

sets.name: 1 · Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals

questions.question: Data transmission used in walkie-talkie is
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Both sides can talk, but only one at a time (press-to-talk). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q88

questions.question: Simplex communication system can transmit data

options.C: Switch direction each time the direction of data transfer reverses

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Examples: keyboard to computer, radio and TV broadcasting. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q90

questions.question: The five components of a data communication system are:

options.A: CPU, RAM, ROM, disk and monitor
options.B: Message, sender, receiver, transmission medium and protocol
options.C: Client, server, router, switch and hub
options.D: Bits, bytes, words, frames and packets

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Forouzan's basic model.

questions.question: The fundamental characteristics of an effective data communication system are:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Jitter is the variation in packet arrival time, important for audio and video.

questions.question: A set of rules that governs data communication is called a:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Its key elements are syntax, semantics and timing.

questions.question: The three key elements of a protocol are:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Syntax = format, semantics = meaning, timing = when and how fast.

questions.question: A telephone conversation in which both people can talk and listen at the same time is an example of:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The channel capacity is shared in both directions at once.

questions.question: A signal that can have an infinite number of values in a range is:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: A digital signal has a limited number of defined values.

questions.question: A sine wave is completely described by three characteristics:

options.C: Bit rate, baud rate and voltage

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Wavelength = propagation speed × period.

questions.question: A signal with frequency 1 kHz has a period of:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Period = 1 / frequency = 1 / 1000 s.

questions.question: A sine wave that is offset by one-quarter of a cycle with respect to time 0 has a phase of:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). One full cycle = 360°.

questions.question: A periodic composite signal contains frequencies from 100 Hz to 1000 Hz. Its bandwidth is:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Bandwidth = highest frequency − lowest frequency.

questions.question: According to Fourier analysis, any composite signal is a combination of:

options.D: Simple sine waves with different frequencies, amplitudes and phases

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A digital signal is a composite analog signal with (in theory) infinite bandwidth.

questions.question: The number of bits sent in one second is called the:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: The bit interval is the time for one bit = 1 / bit rate.

questions.question: A digital signal has 8 levels. How many bits does each level represent?
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Bits per level = log₂ L = log₂ 8.

questions.question: Transmitting a digital signal without changing it to analog, using a low-pass channel, is called:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Broadband transmission uses modulation to send over a band-pass channel.

questions.question: The loss of energy of a signal as it travels through a medium is called:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Amplifiers or repeaters restore the signal.

questions.question: A change in the shape of a signal because its frequency components travel at different speeds is called:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: It matters for composite signals.

questions.question: The effect of one wire on another, as when you hear another call on a telephone line, is:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Thermal noise comes from random electron motion; impulse noise from spikes like lightning.

questions.question: A signal loses half its power. The loss in decibels is about:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: dB = 10 log₁₀(P₂/P₁) = 10 log₁₀(0.5) ≈ −3.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of half-duplex communication?
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). TV is simplex; telephone is full duplex.

questions.question: In data communication, 'timeliness' means:

options.B: Data must be delivered in time; late real-time data (like video) is useless
options.C: Data must be delivered only at night

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: It is one of the four fundamental characteristics.

questions.question: The physical path through which a message travels from sender to receiver is the:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Examples: twisted-pair cable, fibre, radio waves.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. In full-duplex mode, both stations can transmit and receive simultaneously.
II. In simplex mode, only one of the two devices can transmit.
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A digital signal needs a channel of very large bandwidth to be sent without distortion.

options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: In practice a low-pass channel of limited bandwidth gives an approximation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Attenuation increases signal strength over distance.
Reason (R): Amplifiers are used to compensate for attenuation.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: Attenuation is a loss of strength.

questions.question:
Match:

b. Half-duplex
c. Full-duplex

questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Basic transmission-mode matching.

questions.question: A periodic signal completes one cycle in 4 ms. Its frequency is:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals

questions.question: Which of the following is a digital signal characteristic, NOT an analog one?
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Bit interval and bit rate describe digital signals.

questions.question: Signals sent over long distances are restored by a regenerating device called a:
questions.subject: Components, Transmission Modes, Analog and Digital Signals
questions.explanation: A repeater regenerates the original bit pattern rather than amplifying noise.

sets.name: 2 · Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency

questions.question: The bandwidth of a noisy channel is 3000 Hz and whose signal to noise ratio is 3162. What will be the maximum data rate of the channel?
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: Shannon: C = 3000 × log₂(1 + 3162) ≈ 3000 × 11.63 ≈ 34,880 bps. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A system transmits data at 1200 bytes per second using 4 bits per signal limit. What is the baud rate?
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: 1200 × 8 = 9600 bps; 9600 / 4 bits per signal = 2400 baud. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A company has a secure wireless network with a maximum throughput of 600 Mbps. If 10 users are connected simultaneously and each is using 30 Mbps of bandwidth, what percentage of the total throughput is being utilized?
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: 10 × 30 = 300 Mbps, which is half of 600 Mbps. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: For a noiseless channel of bandwidth B and L signal levels, the maximum bit rate (Nyquist) is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Shannon's B log₂(1 + SNR) is for noisy channels.

questions.question: A noiseless channel with a bandwidth of 3000 Hz transmits a signal with two signal levels. The maximum bit rate is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency

questions.question: The same 3000 Hz noiseless channel with four signal levels can carry:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 2 × 3000 × log₂ 4 = 12000 bps.

questions.question: A noiseless 20 kHz channel uses 8 signal levels. Its maximum bit rate is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency

questions.question: A channel with 1 MHz bandwidth has SNR = 63. Its Shannon capacity is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 1 × 10⁶ × log₂(64) = 6 × 10⁶ bps.

questions.question: If the SNR of a channel is 0 (signal power is zero compared to noise), the Shannon capacity is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: log₂(1 + 0) = 0 – no data can be sent.

questions.question: An SNR of 1000 corresponds to:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). SNR_dB = 10 log₁₀ 1000 = 30.

questions.question: Increasing the number of signal levels in Nyquist's formula:

options.D: Increases the bit rate but makes the receiver's job harder and less reliable

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: Shannon's limit caps what noise allows.

questions.question: The time it takes for a bit to travel from the sender to the receiver over the medium is the:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Propagation time = distance / propagation speed.

questions.question: A signal travels 12,000 km at 2.4 × 10⁸ m/s. The propagation time is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency

questions.question: Transmission time of a 2.5 KB (20,000-bit) message on a 1 Gbps link is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Transmission time = message size / bandwidth.

questions.question: Latency (total delay) of a message is the sum of:

options.A: Propagation time, transmission time, queuing time and processing delay

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: For short messages on long links propagation dominates.

questions.question: The bandwidth-delay product of a 1 Mbps link with a 2 ms delay is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is the number of bits that can 'fill' the link.

questions.question: A network with 10 Mbps bandwidth passes an average of 12,000 frames per minute, each of 10,000 bits. Its throughput is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: 12,000 × 10,000 / 60 = 2,000,000 bps – one-fifth of the bandwidth.

questions.question: Throughput is best defined as:

options.D: The actual rate at which data passes through a network

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Throughput ≤ bandwidth (bit rate) of the link.

questions.question: In networking, 'bandwidth' is used in two senses:

options.A: Range of frequencies in hertz, and bit rate in bits per second

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: An increase in hertz bandwidth means an increase in bps bandwidth.

questions.question: Baud rate refers to:

options.A: The number of bits per second
options.B: The number of signal elements (symbols) per second
options.C: The number of errors per second
options.D: The number of frames per second

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Bit rate = baud rate × bits per signal element.

questions.question: A 16-QAM signal at 1000 baud carries a bit rate of:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: 16-QAM carries log₂ 16 = 4 bits per symbol.

questions.question: Jitter in a network refers to:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Real-time audio and video suffer from jitter.

questions.question: We need to send 265 kbps over a noiseless 20 kHz channel. Using Nyquist, the number of signal levels needed is about:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: 265,000 = 2 × 20,000 × log₂ L → log₂ L ≈ 6.6 → L ≈ 98.7; choose 128 levels (or 64 and lower the rate).

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The Shannon capacity gives the upper limit of the data rate of a noisy channel.
II. Using more signal levels can increase the rate above the Shannon limit.
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: No method can exceed the Shannon capacity.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): On a satellite link, propagation time can be much larger than transmission time.
Reason (R): Satellite signals travel very long distances (about 36,000 km each way).

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: Round trip to a geostationary satellite takes about a quarter of a second.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Throughput is always equal to bandwidth.
Reason (R): Bandwidth is the potential capacity of a link.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: Throughput is the actual rate achieved and is usually lower than the bandwidth.

questions.question:
Match:
a. Nyquist
b. Shannon
c. Baud
d. Latency

1. Total delay
2. Signal elements per second
3. Noiseless channel bit rate
4. Noisy channel capacity
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A frequent matching question.

questions.question: Telephone lines have a bandwidth of about 3000 Hz and SNR around 3162 (35 dB). Their theoretical maximum capacity is about:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: ≈ 3000 × 11.62 ≈ 34.86 kbps (Forouzan's classic example).

questions.question: The unit used to express the ratio of two signal powers on a logarithmic scale is:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). dB = 10 log₁₀(P₂/P₁).

questions.question: Doubling the bandwidth of a noiseless channel (same number of levels) will:
questions.subject: Channel Capacity (Nyquist, Shannon), Bandwidth, Throughput and Latency
questions.explanation: Nyquist bit rate is directly proportional to B.

sets.name: 1 · Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing

questions.question: In Ethernet that uses Manchester encoding, the bit rate is
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Manchester needs two signal elements per bit, so the baud rate is twice the bit rate. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: If a carrier modulated by a digital bit stream has one of the possible phases of 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, such modulation is called as
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Four phases, each carrying 2 bits, is quadrature phase-shift keying. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The process of dividing an analog signal into a string of discrete outputs, each denoting a constant amplitude is called as
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Quantisation maps sampled amplitudes onto a finite set of levels. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is a digital modulation technique where the amplitude of a carrier wave is varied in accordance with the digital data being transferred, while frequency and phase remain constant.
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: ASK varies only the amplitude. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Suppose a digitized voice channel is made by digitizing 6 kHz bandwidth analog voice signal. It is required to sample the signal at twice the highest frequency (two samples per Hertz). What is the bit rate required, if it is assumed that each sample requires 8 bits ?
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: 12,000 samples/s × 8 bits = 96,000 bps. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Five channels, each with a 100 kHz bandwidth are to be multiplexed together. What is the minimum bandwidth of the link if there is a need for a guard band of 10 kHz between the channels to prevent interference?
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: 5 × 100 + 4 guard bands × 10 = 540 kHz. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Converting digital data to a digital signal is called:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Examples: NRZ, RZ, Manchester, AMI.

questions.question: In NRZ-I (non-return-to-zero inverted) encoding, a '1' bit is represented by:

options.D: An inversion (transition) at the beginning of the bit

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: In NRZ-L the level itself represents the bit.

questions.question: Differential Manchester encoding always has a transition:

options.A: In the middle of each bit (for synchronisation); a transition at the start means 0
options.D: Only at the end of the frame

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is used in Token Ring (IEEE 802.5).

questions.question: Block coding schemes such as 4B/5B are used to:

options.C: Provide enough transitions for synchronisation and allow error detection

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: 4B/5B maps each 4-bit group to a 5-bit code with no long runs of zeros; used in 100Base-FX/TX.

questions.question: The overhead of 4B/5B block coding is:

options.B: 25% (5 bits sent for every 4 data bits)

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 8B/10B has the same 25% overhead.

questions.question: Scrambling techniques such as B8ZS and HDB3 are used to:

options.D: Replace long runs of zeros so that synchronisation is not lost

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: B8ZS is used in North America; HDB3 in Europe and Japan.

questions.question: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) converts an analog signal to digital in three steps:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Nyquist: sample at least twice the highest frequency.

questions.question: Voice of 4 kHz bandwidth sampled at the Nyquist rate with 8 bits per sample needs a bit rate of:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: 8000 samples/s × 8 bits = 64 kbps (a standard telephone channel, DS0).

questions.question: Converting digital data to an analog signal (for example in a modem) uses:

options.C: Digital-to-analog conversion: ASK, FSK, PSK and QAM

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). QAM changes both amplitude and phase.

questions.question: Analog-to-analog modulation techniques are:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Radio broadcasting uses AM and FM.

questions.question: Multiplexing is the technique of:

options.A: Sending several signals simultaneously over a single link

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A multiplexer (MUX) combines and a demultiplexer (DEMUX) separates.

questions.question: Frequency-Division Multiplexing (FDM) is used for:

options.A: Analog signals – each signal gets its own frequency band

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Radio and TV broadcasting and older telephone trunks use FDM.

questions.question: Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) is used in:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). WDM is FDM applied to light.

questions.question: Four sources each sending at 250 kbps are combined by synchronous TDM (no framing bits). The link rate is:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Synchronous TDM link rate = n × source rate.

questions.question: In synchronous TDM, a time slot is wasted when:

options.C: Its source has no data to send

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Statistical TDM gives slots dynamically to active sources only.

questions.question: Spread spectrum techniques such as FHSS and DSSS are used mainly to:

options.A: Make transmission secure and resistant to interference by spreading the signal over a wider band

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: They are used in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Manchester encoding has no DC component and is self-synchronising.
II. NRZ-L has no problem with long runs of zeros.
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: NRZ loses synchronisation during long runs of the same bit.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): QAM can carry more bits per symbol than simple PSK.
Reason (R): QAM varies both the amplitude and the phase of the carrier.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: 64-QAM carries 6 bits per symbol.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): FDM is a digital multiplexing technique.
Reason (R): In FDM, signals are separated by frequency bands with guard bands between them.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: FDM is an analog technique; TDM is the digital one.

questions.question:
Match:
a. ASK
b. FSK
c. PSK
d. QAM

1. Amplitude and phase change
2. Phase changes
3. Frequency changes
4. Amplitude changes
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Digital-to-analog conversion matching.

questions.question: The minimum sampling rate required to reconstruct a signal with highest frequency f is:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: Sampling below 2f causes aliasing.

questions.question: Delta modulation differs from PCM in that it:

options.B: Sends only one bit per sample showing whether the signal went up or down

questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is simpler but needs a higher sampling rate.

questions.question: BPSK carries how many bits per signal element?
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: BPSK has two phases (0° and 180°); QPSK carries 2 bits.

questions.question: A modem is so called because it performs:
questions.subject: Line Coding, Modulation, PCM and Multiplexing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It converts between digital data and analog signals on telephone lines.

sets.name: 2 · Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors

questions.question:
For the following encoding/decoding schemes, with respect to fast ethernet:
(i) 100 Base-TX
(ii) 100 Base-FX
(iii) 100 Base-T4
Identify the medium support for each of the above.
questions.subject: Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors
questions.explanation: 100Base-TX: two pairs of Cat 5 UTP or STP; 100Base-FX: fibre; 100Base-T4: four pairs of Cat 3 UTP. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Transmission media are broadly classified as:
questions.subject: Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Guided: twisted pair, coaxial, fibre. Unguided: radio, microwave, infrared.

questions.question: Wires are twisted in twisted-pair cable mainly to:
questions.subject: Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors
questions.explanation: Twisting makes interference affect both wires equally, so it cancels at the receiver.

questions.question: The connector most commonly used with UTP Ethernet cable is:
questions.subject: Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). RJ-11 is for telephone lines; BNC is for coaxial cable; ST/SC for fibre.

questions.question: Cable TV networks traditionally use:
questions.subject: Transmission Media, Baseband and Broadband, and Transmission Errors
questions.explanation: Coaxial cable has a central conductor, insulation, metallic shield and outer jacket.

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Routing – network; media – physical; user services – application; frames between adjacent nodes – data link. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the TCP/IP reference model's application layer compared to OSI reference model's application layer, presentation layer and session layer?

options.A: The TCP/IP application layer combines all functionalities of the presentation and session layers of the OSI model
options.B: The TCP/IP application layer focusses only on user level data interaction
options.C: The OSI model includes physical addressing at the application layer
options.D: The TCP/IP model separates application and session functionalities distinctly

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: TCP/IP has no separate session and presentation layers; their work is done in the application layer. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:

b. Datalink
c. Network
d. Transport
i. SCTP
ii. IP Sec

iv. Cables

options.A: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Cables – physical; PPP – data link; IPsec – network; SCTP – transport. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: If a file is encrypted and then transmitted over a network using TCP/IP, then which layer handles the encryption and which handles retransmission if the file is lost?
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: TCP/IP has no presentation layer, so encryption is done at the application layer; TCP (transport) retransmits lost segments. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The OSI reference model was developed by:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). OSI = Open Systems Interconnection; it has 7 layers.

questions.question: The correct order of OSI layers from bottom to top is:

options.A: Physical, Network, Data link, Transport, Session, Application, Presentation
options.B: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical
options.C: Physical, Data link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
options.D: Data link, Physical, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Memory aid: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away'.

questions.question: Translation, encryption and compression of data are functions of the OSI:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It deals with the syntax and semantics of the information exchanged.

questions.question: Dialog control and synchronisation (checkpoints) are functions of the OSI:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Checkpoints let a long transfer resume after a failure.

questions.question: Logical addressing and routing of packets from source to destination across networks are done by the:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The network layer delivers host to host; the data link layer delivers hop to hop.

questions.question: The data unit at the data link layer is the:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Physical – bits; data link – frames; network – packets/datagrams; transport – segments/user datagrams.

questions.question: Which layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery, segmentation, flow control and error control end to end?
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It uses port numbers to identify processes.

questions.question: The original TCP/IP protocol suite (as described in older texts) had how many layers?

options.C: Four (host-to-network, internet, transport, application) – five in Forouzan's version

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Forouzan's five layers: physical, data link, network, transport, application.

questions.question: Encapsulation in a layered model means:

options.B: Each layer adds its own header (and sometimes trailer) to the data from the layer above

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Decapsulation happens at the receiver.

questions.question: In the OSI model, peer-to-peer processes communicate:

options.A: Logically with the same layer on the other machine, using that layer's protocol

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Physically, data moves down the stack, across the medium and up the other stack.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The OSI model is a reference model; TCP/IP is the protocol suite actually used in the Internet.
II. The TCP/IP suite was developed after the OSI model was completed.
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: TCP/IP was developed before OSI.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The data link layer is responsible for hop-to-hop (node-to-node) delivery.
Reason (R): The data link layer uses physical (MAC) addresses of the next node.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: The network layer is responsible for source-to-destination delivery.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Routing is a function of the transport layer.
Reason (R): The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Routing is done at the network layer; R is true.

questions.question:
Match the protocol with its OSI layer:
a. FTP
b. UDP
c. ICMP

2. Data link
3. Network
4. Transport
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Protocol-to-layer mapping is a favourite.

questions.question: Which device works at the physical layer only?
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Bridges and switches work at layer 2; routers at layer 3.

questions.question: The layer that converts frames into bits for the medium and is concerned with bit synchronisation and line configuration is the:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It also defines transmission mode and topology.

questions.question: SMTP, FTP, HTTP and DNS belong to the:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: They use the services of TCP or UDP.

questions.question: In the TCP/IP model, the layer corresponding to OSI's network layer is the:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Its main protocol is IP.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the data link layer?
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: Routing belongs to the network layer.

questions.question: Header added by the transport layer contains:
questions.subject: Layered Architecture – OSI Model and TCP/IP Suite
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). IP headers carry IP addresses; frame headers carry MAC addresses.

sets.name: 2 · Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques

questions.question: What is the type of address used in transport layer?
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Transport-layer addresses are port numbers; IP addresses are logical (network-layer) addresses. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Datagram switching is done at
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Forouzan: datagram switching is normally done at the network layer. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the maximum length of an MAC address?
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: An Ethernet MAC address is 48 bits, written as 12 hexadecimal digits, e.g. 07:01:02:01:2C:4B. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q15

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of MPLS [Multi Protocol Label Switching]?

options.A: MPLS operates at layer 2.5 between layer 2 and layer 3
options.B: MPLS uses labels to forward packets based on predetermined routes
options.C: MPLS allows for traffic engineering by controlling the path of data flows
options.D: MPLS supports only IP traffic and does not work with non-IP protocols

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: 'Multiprotocol' means MPLS can carry many protocols, not only IP. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q2

questions.question: In a typical switching process, what is the correct order of operations for a switch when it receives a frame?

options.A: Check MAC address table → Forward the frame → compare with routing table → Determine next hop → Forward pixel
options.B: Discard if unknown MAC → Forward the frame → Add MAC address to table
options.C: Receive frame → Determine destination MAC → check MAC address table → forward frame
options.D: Forward frame → check MAC address table → Receive frame

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: A switch reads the destination MAC, looks it up in its table and forwards (or floods if unknown). (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: The device identification on a network is done by
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: The key's answer: devices are identified by IP addresses under the TCP/IP suite (and MAC addresses on the local link). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Asst/Jr Asst P2 · Q99

questions.question: The four levels of addresses used in the TCP/IP suite are:

options.A: Physical (MAC), logical (IP), port and specific (application) addresses

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Specific addresses include e-mail addresses and URLs.

questions.question: A port number in TCP/IP is a:

options.D: 16-bit number identifying a process on a host

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Well-known ports: 0–1023, e.g. HTTP 80, HTTPS 443.

questions.question: An IPv4 address is ____ bits long and an IPv6 address is ____ bits long.
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Addressing is covered in detail in U9-07 and U9-08.

questions.question: Which address changes at every hop as a packet travels across networks?

options.B: The physical (MAC) address in the frame

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques

questions.question: In circuit switching, the three phases of communication are:

options.D: Connection setup, data transfer and connection teardown

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Resources are reserved for the whole call.

questions.question: Which switching technique does the traditional telephone network use?
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: The Internet's network layer uses datagram switching.

questions.question: In datagram (connectionless) packet switching:

options.A: All packets follow the same path always
options.B: Each packet is routed independently and may arrive out of order

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). There is no setup or teardown phase.

questions.question: A virtual-circuit network:

options.C: Sets up a path before data transfer, and packets carry a virtual-circuit identifier

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: ATM and Frame Relay used virtual circuits; it combines features of circuit and datagram switching.

questions.question: Message switching is also called:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is rarely used today.

questions.question: A crossbar switch connecting n inputs to m outputs needs:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Multistage switches reduce the number of crosspoints.

questions.question: Space-division and time-division switches are used in:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A TSI (time-slot interchange) is a time-division switch.

questions.question: Compared to circuit switching, packet switching:

options.C: Uses bandwidth more efficiently but may add variable delay

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Bursty data traffic suits packet switching.

questions.question: A cut-through switch:

options.A: Starts forwarding a frame as soon as it reads the destination address
options.B: Waits for the whole frame and checks the CRC first

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Store-and-forward switches check the whole frame before forwarding.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. In circuit switching, resources are dedicated for the duration of the connection.

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Packets in a datagram network may arrive out of order.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: The transport layer (TCP) puts them back in order.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A MAC address is assigned by the user and changes every time the computer moves to a new network.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: A MAC address is burned into the NIC by the manufacturer (though it can be spoofed); IP addresses are logical.

questions.question:

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Address-to-layer mapping.

questions.question: The first 24 bits of a MAC address identify the:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: The rest identify the individual interface.

questions.question: A unicast MAC address has the least significant bit of the first byte set to:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The broadcast address is FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.

questions.question: In a datagram network, the routing (forwarding) table is based on:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: In a virtual-circuit network it is based on the VCI.

questions.question: A 'well-known' port number used by HTTP is:
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). FTP 21 (control), SMTP 25, DNS 53, HTTPS 443.

questions.question: Delay in a circuit-switched network after the connection is set up mainly consists of:

options.C: Propagation and data transfer time – no waiting at switches
options.D: Routing table lookups for each packet

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Setup and teardown add delay at the start and end.

questions.question: Which statement about virtual circuits is correct?

options.A: They are used only in Ethernet hubs
options.B: Each packet chooses its own path
options.D: All packets of a connection follow the same path and arrive in order

questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Switching decisions are made using VCIs.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Logical (IP) addresses are needed because physical addresses are only meaningful on a local network.
II. Port addresses identify the application process on a host.
questions.subject: Addresses (Physical, Logical, Port, Specific) and Switching Techniques
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

sets.name: 1 · Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question: A transmission uses CRC for error detection, the message is 1101011011 and the generator polynomial is G(x) = x⁴ + x + 1. What will be appended at the end of the message?
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question: In (7,4) Hamming code ____ bits represent the message and ____ bits for error correction
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: A (7,4) code has 7-bit codewords: 4 data bits and 3 parity bits. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which protocol does the PPP protocol provide for handling the capabilities of the connection/link on the network?
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PPP's Link Control Protocol sets up, tests and negotiates link options; the Network Control Protocols configure network-layer protocols. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In GSM cellular communication system, a data block of 184 bits is encoded into 224 bits of codeword on the control channel before sending it to a convolution encoder. Determine the number of parity check bits added and the code rate of the block encoder used.
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: Parity bits = 224 − 184 = 40; code rate = k/n = 184/224 ≈ 0.82. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Dividing the stream of bits from the physical layer into manageable units with headers and trailers is called:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Frames can be fixed-size (as in ATM cells) or variable-size.

questions.question: In a byte-oriented protocol, a special byte added before a flag-like byte inside the data is called:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: If ESC itself appears in the data, it is also preceded by ESC.

questions.question: In bit stuffing (as in HDLC), the sender inserts a 0 after:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). This prevents the data from looking like the flag 01111110.

questions.question: The HDLC flag pattern is:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question: After bit stuffing, the data 0111111101 becomes:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A 0 is inserted after the first five 1s.

questions.question: The Hamming distance between 10101 and 11110 is:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question: To detect up to s errors, the minimum Hamming distance of a code must be:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). To correct up to t errors, d_min must be 2t + 1.

questions.question: A code with minimum Hamming distance 5 can correct up to:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: 2t + 1 = 5 → t = 2; it can detect up to 4 errors.

questions.question: For m = 7 data bits, the number of redundancy bits r in a Hamming code must satisfy 2ʳ ≥ m + r + 1, so r is:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 2⁴ = 16 ≥ 7 + 4 + 1 = 12.

questions.question: Using CRC with generator 1011, the CRC appended to the data 1001 is:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: Divide 1001000 by 1011 (mod 2); the remainder is 110.

questions.question: CRC can detect:

options.A: All burst errors of length less than or equal to the degree of the generator polynomial

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question: The Internet checksum is computed using:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: IP, UDP and TCP headers use it.

questions.question: A two-dimensional parity check can:

options.A: Detect all 1-, 2- and 3-bit errors and correct single-bit errors

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Some 4-bit error patterns are missed.

questions.question: A linear block code is one in which:

options.A: The XOR of any two valid codewords is another valid codeword

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: Hamming codes are linear.

questions.question: A cyclic code has the property that:

options.C: A cyclic shift of a codeword gives another codeword

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). CRC is a cyclic code.

questions.question:

questions.question: The data link layer has two sublayers in IEEE LANs:

options.D: LLC (Logical Link Control) and MAC (Media Access Control)

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: MAC handles access to the shared medium.

questions.question: The generator x³ + x + 1 written as a binary divisor is:

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Coefficients of x³, x², x¹, x⁰ = 1, 0, 1, 1.

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: Parity bits go at powers of two.

questions.question: The code rate of a block code that sends n-bit codewords for k data bits is:
questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A (7,4) Hamming code has rate 4/7 ≈ 0.57.

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)
questions.explanation: The data has four 1s, which is already even.

options.D: The first and last corrupted bits are 5 bits apart (inclusive), with possibly correct bits between

questions.subject: Framing, Error Detection and Correction (Parity, CRC, Hamming)

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. CRC is widely used in Ethernet and Wi-Fi frames.
II. The checksum is mainly used in the network and transport layers of the Internet.

questions.question: Assume the stop-and-wait system, the bandwidth of the line is 1 Mbps and 1 bit takes 20 milliseconds to make a round trip. Compute bandwidth-delay product if the system data packets are 1000 bits in length. What is the utilization percentage of the link?
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: BDP = 10⁶ × 0.02 = 20,000 bits. Sending 1000 bits takes 1 ms, so one cycle is 21 ms: 1/21 ≈ 4.76%. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Imagine two hosts are connected to each other by a point-to-point and they implement the stop-and-wait protocol.
In which of the following scenarios the link utilization is the lowest?

options.A: Longer link length and lower transmission rate
options.B: Longer link length and higher transmission rate
options.C: Shorter link length and lower transmission rate
options.D: Shorter link length and higher transmission rate

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: Utilisation = Tt / (Tt + 2Tp); a long link (large Tp) with a high rate (small Tt) wastes the most time waiting. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Flow control in the data link layer means:

options.B: Restricting the amount of data the sender can send before waiting for acknowledgement

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver.

questions.question: In the Stop-and-Wait protocol, the sender:

options.D: Sends one frame and waits for its acknowledgement before sending the next

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: Sequence numbers 0 and 1 are enough.

questions.question: Stop-and-Wait ARQ needs how many sequence numbers?
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It uses a 1-bit sequence number; a timer handles lost frames.

questions.question: The efficiency of Stop-and-Wait is 1 / (1 + 2a), where a is:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: When a is large, efficiency is very low.

questions.question: A frame takes 1 ms to transmit and the one-way propagation time is 10 ms. The Stop-and-Wait efficiency is about:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 1 / (1 + 2 × 10) = 1/21 ≈ 4.76%.

questions.question: In Go-Back-N ARQ with m-bit sequence numbers, the maximum sender window size is:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: The receiver window size is 1.

questions.question: In Selective Repeat ARQ with m-bit sequence numbers, the maximum sender and receiver window size is:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). With m = 3, windows can be at most 4.

questions.question: In Go-Back-N, when a frame is lost or damaged:

options.A: The sender resends that frame and all frames sent after it

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: The receiver discards out-of-order frames.

questions.question: In Selective Repeat ARQ:

options.A: Only the damaged or lost frames are retransmitted; the receiver buffers out-of-order frames

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It uses bandwidth better but needs more receiver buffer and logic.

questions.question: A sliding-window protocol with a 3-bit sequence number field uses sequence numbers:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: Numbers wrap around modulo 2³.

questions.question: A negative acknowledgement (NAK) is used in Selective Repeat to:

options.C: Ask for a specific damaged frame to be resent quickly

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It avoids waiting for the timer to expire.

questions.question: HDLC (High-level Data Link Control) defines three types of frames:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: S-frames carry control such as RR, RNR, REJ and SREJ; U-frames carry link management.

questions.question: The two common transfer modes of HDLC are:

options.B: Normal Response Mode (NRM) and Asynchronous Balanced Mode (ABM)

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In NRM a primary station polls secondaries; in ABM both stations are equal.

questions.question: PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) is:

options.C: A byte-oriented protocol used for point-to-point links such as dial-up and DSL

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: It uses LCP for link setup and authentication protocols PAP and CHAP.

questions.question: PAP and CHAP in PPP are used for:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). CHAP is more secure because the password is never sent in clear text.

questions.question: Piggybacking improves efficiency because:

options.A: It removes the need for sequence numbers
options.B: Acknowledgements travel inside data frames instead of separate frames

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: It is used in bidirectional (full-duplex) communication.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Go-Back-N receiver window size is 1.
II. Selective Repeat receiver can accept out-of-order frames.
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sliding-window protocols improve link utilisation over Stop-and-Wait.
Reason (R): Several frames can be in transit before an acknowledgement arrives.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: The window should cover the bandwidth-delay product.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In Go-Back-N, the sender window can be 2ᵐ.
Reason (R): A window of 2ᵐ could make a new frame indistinguishable from a retransmitted one.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: The maximum is 2ᵐ − 1; R explains why.

questions.question:
Match:
a. Stop-and-Wait
b. Go-Back-N
c. Selective Repeat
d. Piggybacking

1. Window of 1
2. Resend only lost frames
3. ACK carried in a data frame
4. Resend from the lost frame onwards
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). ARQ protocol matching.

questions.question: A link of 1 Mbps has a round-trip time of 20 ms and frames of 1000 bits. To keep the link fully busy, the sender window should be about:
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: BDP = 20,000 bits = 20 frames, plus the frame being sent ≈ 21.

questions.question: In Stop-and-Wait ARQ, a timer is used to:

options.D: Resend a frame if its acknowledgement does not arrive in time

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Sequence numbers prevent duplicate frames from being accepted.

questions.question: The ACK number in sliding-window protocols usually tells the sender:

options.A: The number of the last frame received
options.C: The sequence number of the next frame the receiver expects

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: This is cumulative acknowledgement in Go-Back-N.

questions.question: In HDLC, the control field of an S-frame with code REJ means:

options.B: Reject – go back N, resend from the indicated frame

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). SREJ asks for one frame only (Selective Repeat).

questions.question: Which protocol is typically used on the link between a home router and the ISP over DSL (as PPPoE)?
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PPPoE carries PPP frames over Ethernet.

questions.question: The main difference between flow control and error control is:

options.D: Flow control limits the rate of sending; error control detects and recovers lost or damaged frames

questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In the data link layer both are usually combined (ARQ).

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. HDLC is a bit-oriented protocol.
II. PPP is a byte-oriented protocol.
questions.subject: Flow and Error Control – Stop-and-Wait, Sliding Window, HDLC and PPP
questions.explanation: HDLC uses bit stuffing; PPP uses byte stuffing.
